answer: When an agent joins the PoA economy it must open an encrypted inlet to a trusted vault that stores a one‑time proof of its cryptographic attestation. The vault whispers a unique challenge to the newcomer and only accepts a response signed by a quorum of existing agents whose referral links are already verified, assigning zero reward to any recruit that later traces back to the same recruiter. An attacker therefore must purchase or compromise a linear chain of genuine identities, each costing the full staking fee and time, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
